title: Incident records, complaints and safeguarding response
audience: Tutors and education coaches (draft shell, no teaching content yet)
learningOutcomes: Write an incident record that states the facts, the time, the people involved and the action taken, without guesses or opinion.
Handle a complaint through a set route, by acknowledging it, checking the facts and recording the outcome.
Respond to a safeguarding concern by following the reporting route and sharing information only with the people who need it.

instruction.heading: What an incident record contains
instruction.body: An incident record should give the date and time, the place, the people involved, what was seen or heard, what was done in response, and who was told. Keep facts separate from opinions, and write the words used by any person as closely as possible. Do not alter a record after it has been written. If something needs correcting or adding later, make a dated addition that shows who wrote it. Sign and date each record at the time it is made.

instruction.heading: Handling a complaint
instruction.body: Acknowledge each complaint in writing within the time the business has stated. Listen to the complaint, check the facts against the session record, and decide what can be done within the scope the business has set. Do not promise a refund, a discount or a remedy unless the business owner has approved it in writing. Record the complaint, the facts checked, the outcome and the reply sent. If the client is not satisfied, explain how the complaint can be escalated, and record that too.

instruction.heading: Responding to a safeguarding concern
instruction.body: A safeguarding concern may come from a disclosure by a child, something the tutor has seen, or a statement by an adult. If a child is in immediate danger, call emergency services first. Do not promise a child that what they tell you will be kept secret. Record the child's words as they were said, with the date and time. Do not question the child beyond what is needed to understand what was said. Tell the business owner at once and follow the reporting route confirmed by the expert reviewer, as set out in NEW-TUT-02.

instruction.heading: Keeping records private
instruction.body: Keep incident, complaint and safeguarding records in the business's recorded system, with access limited to people who need them to act on the record. Do not discuss a safeguarding concern with the client or the wider family unless the reporting route requires it. How long these records must be kept, and what privacy rules apply to them, are UNCONFIRMED in this lesson and must be set by the business owner with the reviewer.
